native_name: 川崎重工業株式会社 (Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Ltd.)

selection.reason: Japan's other heavy-industry prime: P-1 patrol and C-2 transport aircraft, the OH-1 helicopter, submarines, rolling stock, motorcycles and industrial robots. The game's sourced 1990 industrial-robotics technology for Japan already names Kawasaki Heavy Industries, so this dossier extends an existing reference.

existing_game_references.note: Evidence text names Kawasaki Heavy Industries among 1990 robot builders.

summary: KHI has carried its name since 1939 and was operating across ships, aircraft and rolling stock in 1990. It split off shipbuilding (Kawasaki Shipbuilding Corporation) and precision machinery in October 2002, and the plant business in April 2005, and merged all three back in October 2010; it spun off KCM in 2009 and sold it to Hitachi Construction Machinery in 2015. In October 2021 rolling stock became Kawasaki Railcar Manufacturing and motorcycles and engines Kawasaki Motors, of which KHI sold 20% on 1 April 2025 (ITOCHU took the stake). Products in the window include the first production P-1 (2013) and C-2 (2016), the OH-1 (first flight 1996), the submarine Hakugei (2023), Boeing 787 forward fuselages, Shinkansen and export trains, the Ninja H2 (2015) and industrial robots.

proposed.uncertainty: The existing 1990 evidence names KHI among robot builders; the link is identity only and grants no mechanic.
Generated contractors are fictional; rolling stock, motorcycles and robots have no product consumer, so a real identity would only replace one generated manufacturing contractor.

KHI defence products (patrol and transport aircraft, helicopters, submarines, missiles) have no designer platform; a defense contractor slot is the only service route, and MHI is proposed for the same sector.

duplicates_avoided: Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha (K Line, 1919) and Kawasaki Steel (1950) were separated before the window and are not KHI businesses.
Kawasaki Shipbuilding Corporation (2002-2010 subsidiary) is not the 1896 founding company 株式会社川崎造船所.
Kawasaki Railcar Manufacturing (2021) is not the historic 川崎車輌 merged into KHI in 1969; Kawasaki Motors, Ltd. (2021) is not Kawasaki Motors Corp., U.S.A.
Hakugei is attributed to KHI and the lead boat Taigei to MHI; the OH-1 engines are MHI products.
Medicaroid is a joint venture with Sysmex and NACKS a joint venture with COSCO; neither is a wholly owned KHI unit.

integration_flow.summary: A later, reviewed integration could attach this sourced identity to a company created through the existing orders. Design stays with the commissioning country; Defense R&D pays development as work is performed; the company funds tooling, national-warehouse inputs and fabrication from its own settled cash; the buyer purchases whole finished units from company stock; delivery follows fiscal settlement and seven accessible days. KHI products in this dossier have no designer platform, so a reviewed integration would first need new platform families (a later ruling), not a scripted product.

steps.note: Paid capitalisation from Defense procurement (political capital price applies); leases one existing completed Arms Plant slot. No historical factory, balance or stock is granted.
Further paid working capital; unsettled receivables are not spendable cash.
Frozen design revision; Defense R&D pays engineering, prototype and trials work day by day; prototypes are never saleable.
Finite company-owned stock target (0-12 units); a target is never a government order.
Government buys whole units from existing company stock; settlement then seven accessible delivery days.

unmapped: P-1 and C-2: no maritime-patrol or airlift platform in the designer.
OH-1 and the middle-range multi-purpose missile: no helicopter or vehicle-missile platform.
Hakugei: the only submarine kit (aip_ssk) assumes air-independent propulsion, which MHI does not describe for this class.
Rolling stock, motorcycles, robots and Boeing aerostructures: no civilian product consumer.

gaps: The KHI corporate history and timeline pages returned HTTP 403 and are recorded as inaccessible.
The official chronology and the securities report disagree on the date of the crusher-business transfer (2003 joint venture versus April 2005); it is not recorded.
Kawasaki Motors dates the Ninja H2/H2R to 2014 in its own history, while the KHI chronology gives the 2015 launch used here.
The first P-1 and C-2 export or later production figures were not researched.

future_policy.note: Nothing after the frozen cutoff is predicted. Any later product, successor or business in a campaign must be authored as explicitly fictional game content (labelled "(fictional)") or left unknown.
